title: Evening snag + hypothesis dump (midshift)
content:
Topline: short shift, hit a subtle p99 tail around 23:15 UTC. Recording immediate observations, quick hypotheses, and next actions before I sleep. Treat as personal log / working notes — will refine into ticket text tomorrow.

What happened (timeline):
- 22:30 UTC: normal traffic; sustained throughput ~420 qps across pool-shard-7.
- 23:13 UTC: small cluster of requests to model-cascade-13 caused p99 jump from 85ms -> 420ms for ~3 mins.
- 23:13-23:17: error rate stable, no increase in 5xx, only latency. No obvious CPU/GPU saturation on metrics.
- 23:18: kube autoscaler adjusted a node (scale event correlates, but lag seems bigger than autoscaler delay).

Immediate raw signals I pulled: (ran quick queries against loki / observability)
- top routes: /v1/stream (model-cascade-13) showed more prefix-cache-misses than expected (cache hit rate dropped 18% over baseline).
- per-GPU mem: stable at ~72% across nodes; GPU utilization steady ~38% (so not a hot GPU compute problem).
- host-level load: a handful of nodes had scheduler steal events and sys overhead higher than usual (avg 12% -> peaked 28%).
- nvml counters: context-switches per process spiked on three hosts (could be CUDA context thrash).

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) KV-cache eviction cascade: incoming requests touched many different prefixes (model-cascade-13 route is bursty) and we hit a pathological eviction pattern that invalidated commonly used KV pages, causing more model decoding work and IO. Evidence: cache-hit drop and latency spike without GPU saturation.
2) NUMA / CUDA pinning mismatch during node scale: new pods landed on nodes with different NUMA zones; our cuda-pinning script may have failed to bind GPU thread pools consistently -> context-switch thrash. Evidence: scheduler steal + nvml context switch spikes.
3) I/O stall from ephemerally high metadata ops: small but very frequent calls to storage for model metadata/weights (observed higher S3 GET rate for model-cascade-13 meta objects). Could increase tail if rate-limits or transient throttling.
4) Runtime scheduler bug when batch sizes change quickly: our dynamic batching might shrink/grow and leave stale work items -> increased latency for some in-flight requests. Less evidence but plausible given route is bursty.

Quick attempts and notes: (what I ran locally/cluster)
- curl to internal /health endpoints on affected pod -> all OK.
- rolled restart of single pod in pool-shard-7 -> latency normalized for that shard for ~2 mins then drifted back. Suggests per-pod state contributes.
- toggled kv-cache telemetry (more granular) for next sampling window.
- tried repro with controlled burst (wrk): reproduced small p99 bump but smaller amplitude than prod (hard to fully reproduce workload shape).

Immediate next actions (short):
- [P0] Add targeted debug spans on KV eviction path to capture eviction candidate list for model-cascade-13 requests (Marcus to help with safe flag).
- [P0] Pin suspect pod scheduling to single NUMA zone and observe; add node-level label experiment for one node to force same NUMA alignment. (I'll run tomorrow morning 06:30 UTC).
- [P1] Create an observability alert for rapid drop in kv-cache hitrate (>10% drop over 1m) in addition to latency alerts.
- [P1] Add backlog ticket to quantify S3 GET rate for model-metadata per route (LRN-482 exists but needs owner).
- [P2] Draft micro-benchmark harness that replays request-key-distribution for model-cascade-13 (needs ~1h to script).

Longer-term ideas (brainstorm, may be separate PRDs):
- Eviction-aware warmup: when a model route sees a burst, pre-warm its most-likely KV pages using a small prefetch set derived from recent traces (TTL-based). Could cut tail for bursty routes.
- Per-route cache isolation profiles: allocate soft quota of KV-cache slots to heavy hitters to reduce eviction cascade.
- Improve node admission to prefer pods that have same model hot-set colocated to avoid cross-node S3 metadata pressure.
- Replace some metadata GETs with small consolidated manifest calls to reduce GET storm.

Unresolved questions / unknowns:
- Why did GPU context-switch counters spike even though util is low? Are we running too many CUDA contexts per pod when batching is low?
- Did autoscaler event cause transient scheduling across NUMA that our pinning agent didn't reconcile? Logs from pinning agent are noisy for that timeframe.

What I want from reviewers when I make tickets:
- Help confirm whether eviction telemetry + prefetch idea is straightforward or if it conflicts with other cache invariants.
- SRE: guidance on safe experiment for pinning and node label tests.
- Observability: propose metrics and dashboards for per-route KV eviction waterfall (visualize evictor -> rehydrate -> decode cost).

Standup notes (tomorrow):
- Brief: saw p99 spike on model-cascade-13. Hypothesis: eviction cascade + NUMA pin mismatch. Plan: short experiments (pinning + extra kv telemetry) and create alert for kv-hit drop.

Misc commands / snippets I used (dumped here so I don't forget):
- kubectl -n runtime logs -l app=serving-runtime -c runtime --since=30m | grep "evict" | tail -n 200
- python tools/kv_trace_query.py --route model-cascade-13 --since 24h --out /tmp/kvdump.json
- aws s3api list-objects-v2 --bucket redwood-models --prefix model-cascade-13/meta/ --query 'Contents[].{Key:Key,Size:Size}'

Sleep notes: will start with the pinning experiment and kv telemetry next shift. If anyone is poking at this after me: please leave a short note in the slack thread I created (linked above) with any quick observations so I can pick up tomorrow.

-- Rohan G.
